AIRCRAFT WAS IN MAINTENANCE TO HAVE THE MAIN LANDING GEAR INSPECTED DUE TO PRIOR ISSUES NOTED ON OUR OTHER AIRCRAFT. PER OUR REQUEST, AIRCRAFT WAS PLACED ON JACKS AND THE LANDING GEAR WAS CYCLED TO SEE IF THERE WERE ANY ISSUES, IE; BINDING OR NOISES COMING FROM THE MAIN LANDING GEAR TRUNNIONS WHILE GEAR WAS BEING EXTENDED AND RE-TRACKED. TEXTRON AVIATION ORLANDO SERVICE CENTER MAINTENANCE TECHNICIANS NOTED THAT BOTH MAIN LANDING GEAR FORWARD TRUNNION PIVOT BEARINGS APPEARED TO BE SEIZED, WHICH IS CAUSING RESISTANCE/BINDING AND NOISE WHEN RETRACTING AND EXTENDING THE MAIN LANDING GEAR. MAINTENANCE CREWS ATTEMPTED TO GREASE THESE TWO FORWARD TRUNNION BEARINGS, HOWEVER ONLY ONE SIDE INITIALLY WOULD ACCEPT GREASE. AFTER SOME EFFORT, THE SECOND SIDE STARTED ACCEPTING GREASE. ONCE BOTH MAIN LANDING GEAR FORWARD PIVOT BEARINGS WERE GREASED, THE NOISE AND BINDING OF THE TRUNNIONS DECREASED WHEN CYCLING THE GEAR. IT WAS  THE ORLANDO SERVICE CENTER THEN REMOVED BOTH MAIN LANDING GEAR TRUNNION ASSEMBLIES FROM THE AIRCRAFT TO INSPECT THE FORWARD PIVOT BEARINGS AND PIVOT PINS. AFTER REMOVAL OF BOTH TRUNNIONS, THE LEFT FORWARD BEARING/PIVOT PIN WERE SEIZED TOGETHER. AND AFTER SEVERAL HOURS, THE OLD PIN AND PIVOT BEARING WERE REMOVED. THE MAIN LANDING GEAR ASSEMBLIES WERE REINSTALLED WITH NEW FORWARD TRUNNION PIVOT BEARING AND PIVOT PINS. NOTE: LUBRICATION INTERVAL PER THE TEXTRON AVIATION 525C MM FOR THIS BEARING IS ONCE EVERY 12 MONTHS, THIS AIRCRAFT IS APPROXIMATELY 8 MONTHS OLD.

DURING TAKEOFF FROM BLUE GRASS AIRPORT (KLEX), THE PILOT REPORTED THAT UPON RETRACTING THE LANDING GEAR, THE LANDING GEAR LEVER RED UNSAFE LIGHT ILLUMINATED, ACCOMPANIED BY AN AURAL GEAR WARNING. THE PILOT EXTENDED THE LANDING GEAR, WHICH RESULTED IN THREE DOWN-AND-LOCKED INDICATIONS. HOWEVER, WHEN ATTEMPTING TO LOWER THE FLAPS, THE PILOT NOTED THAT THE FLAP MOTOR CIRCUIT BREAKER HAD POPPED.   THE AIRCRAFT WAS PLACED ON JACKS FOR A GEAR RETRACTION TEST, DURING WHICH MAINTENANCE VERIFIED THE SAME GEAR UNSAFE WARNING LIGHT AND AURAL WARNING. THE FLAP MOTOR CIRCUIT BREAKER WAS OBSERVED TO POP APPROXIMATELY 20 SECONDS AFTER BEING RESET ON THE GROUND. TROUBLESHOOTING REVEALED THAT UNPLUGGING THE CANNON PLUG FROM THE FLAP SWITCH BOX IN THE RIGHT WING FLAP-WELL ELIMINATED THE WARNING AND PREVENTED THE CIRCUIT BREAKER FROM POPPING. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE FLAP WARNING POSITION SWITCH, WHICH ACTIVATES THE GEAR WARNING WHEN FLAPS ARE EXTENDED, WAS STUCK IN THE DOWN POSITION, CAUSING A FALSE GEAR UNSAFE INDICATION AND TRIPPING THE FLAP CIRCUIT BREAKER.   NEW FLAP WARNING POSITION SWITCH (P/N: BZ7RW82255518T) AND FLAP MOTOR (P/N: 101-384040, S/N: 4221) WERE INSTALLED AND RIGGED. SUBSEQUENT TESTING CONFIRMED PROPER GEAR RETRACTION WITHOUT WARNINGS, AND THE FLAP MOTOR CIRCUIT BREAKER NO LONGER TRIPPED.  THE AIRCRAFT WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE FOLLOWING SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF ALL TESTS AND VERIFICATION OF PROPER OPERATION.
